_comment_family: Garamond Premier Pro is an optical-size family: the same design drawn
four times over for four sizes - Caption, the text cut, Subhead and
Display - and then crossed with the weights and the italics. This file
is one cell of that grid, the Bold Italic of the Subhead optical size,
and which cell it is has to be said out loud twice over.
Its name ID 1 is 'Garamond Premr Pro Subh' - Adobe's own abbreviation,
and the name every weight and both slopes of the Subhead size carry.
Its typographic family, name ID 16, is 'Garamond Premier Pro', which
all four optical sizes carry as well. Either of those, declared here,
would be a name several files can answer to, and on a family drawn per
size the wrong answer is not a variation on the design: a Caption cut
is drawn with sturdier hairlines and wider spacing for small sizes and
a Display cut with fine ones for large, so a caption measured against
this file and set from another would be a different colour of type at
a width nothing measured.
So the full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared, exactly as the two
Telegraf packs and american-typewriter-itc-pro-bold declare theirs,
and it is the longest name in this folder because it is the shortest
one that names this file and no other.
Weight 700, which is the file's own usWeightClass and what the cut is
called. The file's macStyle says bold AND italic, which is the second
half of the story and is dealt with below.
Registered at style normal on purpose, the same way open-sans-italic,
hanken-grotesk-italic and rift are. The slant is drawn into the
letterforms - this is a true italic with its own single-storey a, its
own descenders and its own fitting, not a slanted roman - and the
canvas asks for normal. Declaring the FACE italic here as well would
leave the canvas either missing it or being handed a synthetic oblique
of something else. Normal means 'this file, as drawn'.
family: Garamond Premier Pro Bold Italic Subhead
file: fonts/Garamond Premier Pro Bold Italic Subhead.otf
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cell of the grid rather than the family, so a machine
answering to either is answering with this file. Neither 'Garamond
Premier Pro' nor 'Garamond Premr Pro Subh' is here, for the reason
above: they are names four optical sizes and every weight of one of
them answer to, and the local() route is exactly where a name that
loose does its damage - it is tried on whatever the machine happens to
have installed rather than on anything this repo ships.
local: Garamond Premier Pro Bold Italic Subhead
_comment_metrics: Two measurements, both of them for the pack that is set in this face
(content/channels/buzzer-beater-de) and neither of them read by
anything at run time. They are here because the next face dropped
into a Snapchat channel will want the same two taken, and korolev-bold
started the habit.
The cap height is the file's own sCapHeight. The widths were taken on
a canvas at the size the pack is set at, which is the measurement that
matters rather than a sum of advance widths: the renderer measures the
same way, so the numbers below have the kerning in them.
Capitals are 660 units of a 1000-unit em, so at the Snapchat preset's
stated 40px they stand 26.4px tall.
It is a WIDE face for its era, which is the surprise. Twenty mixed
capitals (A to T) come out 499px against the 486px a Snapchat line
has - Korolev Bold's come out 434 - so unlike every other pack under
that heading, the width and the preset's twenty-character ceiling land
in the same place here rather than the characters binding first
comfortably. Ordinary prose still fits: nineteen characters of real
sentence measure 433px, because the spaces and the narrow letters that
an alphabet run has none of do most of the work. What it means in
practice is that a line of unusually wide capitals breaks at nineteen
instead of twenty, which the wrapper does on its own and nobody sees
(see the two ceilings in js/caption.js).
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and here they must be
chosen against the grain of this folder: most of the faces here fall
back through Impact and Arial Black because most of them are heavy
display grotesques, and this is an old-style serif italic. Falling
back to Impact would make the one thing that survives a missing file
the furthest possible thing from it.
So, the nearest garaldes a Windows machine may have: Adobe Garamond
Pro where a design machine carries one, Monotype's Garamond where
Office put one there, and Georgia - which is on every Windows there
is and is at least a serif with bracketed serifs on it - before the
generic. All of them come out upright, because the face is registered
at style normal and there is nothing left to slant it. That is a
caption in the wrong face either way; this only decides what a broken
